subject.title: [security] Unauthenticated OAuth pending queue exhaustion blocks GitHub login

question: What throttling or partitioning policy should Crabbox enforce before unauthenticated GitHub OAuth start requests allocate pending-login records?
rationale: The vulnerable source path is clear, but the fix shape affects the supported unauthenticated login bootstrap and may depend on Worker-compatible caller identity, external edge rate limiting, and operator configurability.

options.title: Per-caller pending limit
options.body: Add a Worker-compatible per-caller or per-device pending-login bucket, keep a guarded global cap, and cover both CLI and portal login paths with regression tests.

options.title: Configurable global-only cap
options.body: Expose the global pending cap and expiry as operator configuration, accepting that anonymous callers may still consume the shared pool without a stronger caller partition.

options.title: Require upstream protection
options.body: Document that public coordinators must place OAuth start routes behind Cloudflare Access or edge rate limiting, leaving Crabbox core behavior mostly unchanged.

recommendation.title: Per-caller pending limit
recommendation.body: Add a Worker-compatible per-caller or per-device pending-login bucket, keep a guarded global cap, and cover both CLI and portal login paths with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Merged OAuth hardening PRs and current-code history make this the best available code-history owner for the policy choice.
